newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen inching up, still bearish.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen inching up, still bearish.

text.p: NOV Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures could inch up slightly on Tuesday in a correction to Monday's slide but technical analysts said the downtrend remained intact.
Traders called the market to open $20 higher on the back of mostly firmer New York prices on Monday.
Darren Gurner, a technical analyst at Sucden, said Monday's break-out to a low of $1,445 was a confirmation of a bear trend which developed since early June.
"We are likely to see prices heading sideways to lower," he said.
The immediate support is pegged at $1,400.
On the upside, the initial resistance is seen at $1,500, followed by $1,545 and the trendline at $1,561. The main upward objective is the August 6 high of $1,678.
"But there's quite a bit of resistance," Gurner said.
On the fundamental front, truck drivers' of Colombia's main transport union declared a strike at the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura in protest at low freight rates, a union official said Monday.
The action began late Saturday but went largely unnoticed given that it came on a three-day bank holiday week-end.
Sources at the port, which handles about 60 percent of all Colombia's incoming and outbound foreign trade, including key coffee exports, said operations were not affected.
Officials of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), however, contested those claims, saying that nothing was being on- or off-loaded to trucks at the port, including coffee and sugar.

Traders were also keeping an eye on the possible squeeze in New York's September contract, political tension in Kenya and the size of the Brazilian crop. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
